summary: Poland is part of the EU and the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, nationals of the countries whose exemption on the EU's visa-exempt list is in force can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90 for adults.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The Schengen Borders Code counts the day you arrive as the first day of stay and the day you leave as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: the Schengen Borders Code counts the 180-day period preceding each day of stay, so days already spent anywhere in the area during that period still count against the 90.

declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and/or photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders, and passports are no longer stamped. Registration happens at the border on your first crossing since the EES started; the EU says it can be quicker if you register some data in advance at a self-service kiosk or through a mobile app, where available. The UK government's travel advice says there is no cost for EES registration.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Poland — days spent in Germany or Czechia count against the same allowance.

The UK government's travel advice says unofficial taxi drivers often overcharge and passengers have been attacked in unofficial taxis and ride-share cars; official taxis show the company's name and phone number on the door and roof. Canada's advice adds that official taxis display the rate per kilometre on the rear passenger window and must have a working meter.
EES registration happens at the border on your first crossing; the EU says it can be quicker if you register some data in advance at a self-service kiosk or through a mobile app, where available.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Poland?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Poland and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS starts, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Poland Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries, and applications are decided within 15 calendar days, a period that may be extended up to 45 days in individual cases.

faq.question: Can Ukrainian citizens enter Poland without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Holders of Ukrainian biometric passports can enter visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period.

faq.question: Does Poland use the euro?
faq.answer: No. Canada's travel advice says the currency of Poland is the zloty (PLN).

faq.question: How long can I stay in Poland without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area.
